messages:
maria_ops: seeing a spike of apiserver 503s in eu-west1 starting ~09:12 UTC. controller-manager leader flips twice in 3m. not sure if etcd or network. anyone oncall? :eyes:
kevin_sre: i pulled metrics — etcd rtt spiked to ~600ms and leader-change count jumped. also nvme_io_wait on cp-4 around the same time.
kevin_sre: snippet from top: ```iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00  0.00 5.00 200.00  1000 40000  201.00    12.2  56.4  5.00 99.9
```
alex_infra: fyi the GPU autoscaler kicked and we had ~18 rtx nodes boot in parallel between 09:00-09:10. kubelets do a lot of list/watch churn when they come up. that could amplify apiserver fd use.
lia_network: check SNAT pool usage — we had a recent change to nat autoscale at 08:45 for eu-west1. there were reports of conntrack spike earlier. i'm checking conntrack counts now.
lia_network: conntrack on nat-1 shows growth to 260k (limit 262k) at 09:11, then several pods start to see conntrack drops. suspect SNAT exhaustion -> retries -> apiserver fanout.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: release/optimize-gpu-onboard rolled to eu-west1 @ 09:05 UTC (sha: ab12f3)
jordan_sre: if conntrack is hitting limits, that explains 503s. controller-manager leader flips could be caused by keepalives failing to reach apiserver. we should: reduce node onboarding parallelism, increase nat pool size, and bump conntrack max if safe.
kevin_sre: agree. also etcd IO stall + apiserver fd pressure is a dangerous combo. adding more SNAT won't help if etcd hammered by watches. we should throttle kube-proxy/kubelet list intervals on boot.
maria_ops: can we triage quickly: lia — can you temp bump conntrack and add one extra nat gateway? alex — can you pause the autoscaler or limit onboarding concurrency? kevin — start a short etcd profile to see compaction/leader metrics?
lia_network: bumping nf_conntrack_max to 400k on nat-1, provisioning extra nat gateway now. will update in 2-3m.
alex_infra: switching gpu-autoscaler to staged mode (max parallel onboards -> 3) and draining 6 of the freshly started nodes to stagger rejoin. doing now.
kevin_sre: running etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd-eu:2379 perf and fetching leader histogram. also increasing apiserver file-descriptor softlimit on controlplane pods as stopgap.
ci-bot: alert: apiserver 503 incidents suppressed (auto) at 09:18 UTC by temporary mitigation flag.
jordan_sre: long-term mitigation ideas: 1) cap node onboarding concurrency for heavy nodes (gpu/ryzen) 2) add a dedicated SNAT pool for controlplane-proxy traffic 3) tune kubelet bootstrap watch backoff 4) increase controller-manager leader lease to 30s in high-latency regions.
maria_ops: thanks. creating incident ticket for postmortem: INF-2026-142. assign kevin & lia for initial RCA. i'll keep this thread for notes. :thumbsup:
kevin_sre: preliminary takeaway: root cause = concurrent GPU node onboarding -> burst of watch/list traffic + conntrack exhaustion on NAT -> increased retries and apiserver fd pressure, amplified by ephemeral nvme IO stalls on the controlplane leading to etcd latency -> leader elections. fix rollout: short-term = conntrack bump + staged onboarding. long-term = throttling + SNAT capacity + controlplane fd tuning.
maria_ops: monitoring looks stable at 09:22, apiserver 5xx rate dropped to baseline. closing incident channel when we have RCA writeup.
alex_infra: noted cost tradeoff — dedicating extra NAT capacity increases cost ~0.6% monthly for eu-west1 but prevents whole-region outages during onboarding surges. will include in PR.
jordan_sre: will draft postmortem template sections and link evaluation prompts to Redwood Optimize to simulate onboarding load.
maria_ops: ok team, great quick response. assigning follow-ups in INF-2026-142.
